allocation_guidance.capacity_authority: Private Aegis authority and the current authorized Calendar amendment own exact reservations, company/degree allocation and the overall capacity limit.
allocation_guidance.introductory_week: Selected beginner essentials end Sunday October 11, 2026. October 3 is the existing on-ramp; October 5–11 is the main sprint. Begin with orientation, then use the curated prerequisite sequence and immediate exercises, without requiring every lesson or repeated drill. No inherited credit or assumed mastery. From October 12, start each studio with a project behavior and use focused lessons for specific gaps; no whole-course restart.

agent_allocation.funding: Reassigned from existing endr morning reservations; not added workload. First-week company setup exceptions follow private active authority.

allocation_guidance.finals_period_policy: No blanket finals-period reduction. Preserve actual classes, examinations and assessment deadlines under private active authority; retain exact resume points and create no catch-up debt.

rules: Selected beginner essentials end Sunday October 11, 2026. October 3 is the existing on-ramp; October 5–11 is the main sprint. Begin with orientation, then use the curated prerequisite sequence and immediate exercises, without requiring every lesson or repeated drill. No inherited credit or assumed mastery. From October 12, start each studio with a project behavior and use focused lessons for specific gaps; no whole-course restart.
Rust receives the largest language allocation; Python and agents start in parallel in the first seven days.

From October 12, project-led practice inside existing reservations: attempt the next unproved behavior; use a focused 20–30 minute explanation when blocked, apply it immediately, then record the exact gap. Do not stretch introductory course consumption across a month. P0 gates remain evidence-based.
Each course/project studio lasts 2–3 hours including short breaks; technical readings last one hour.
Courses and references support the current output. No mandatory completion of every provider exercise, optional project or roadmap node.
The first-50 freshly observed Rustlings gate remains, but drills occur inside Rust hours and do not replace independent CLI proof.
One weekly pair_cycle_id binds Python and Rust work on identical fixtures; independent per-language proof precedes parity.
Keep the agreed UTF-8, ASCII-whitespace, LF, byte-count, stdout/stderr and exit-status Project 0 contract; do not silently loosen it.
Agent/research/domain study earns no Foundation implementation credit and no later-phase, company deployment, weapons or operational authority.

O'Reilly and Coursera subscriptions were user-confirmed active 2026-10-02; four selected Coursera enrollments and the primary Python playlist entry were verified October 2; other item access and API credits remain unverified. Substitute an official reference for the same concept if unavailable; purchase is not required.

Active course selections use O'Reilly or Coursera only. Duke Rust Fundamentals replaces the retired Udemy primary; preserve historical exercises and do not replay Invaders. Current Rust Book guidance resolves tooling/edition questions.
Vanderbilt's coded API examples require paid access; manual traces and stubbed tools avoid making API use an introductory prerequisite.
Course certificates, checked tasks, reservations and zero-collected-test commands are not implementation proof.
End a coding studio with artifact, working directory, command, exit code, observed output, changed paths, verdict, blocker and next command.
Preserve historical work and pre-existing dirty files; this plan authorizes no commit, push, publication or destructive cleanup.
Optional official videos belong inside an existing studio, never as a second workload.
Roadmap navigation uses the existing weekly review, not extra mandatory course blocks.
Official documentation is implementation reference, not a course or extra syllabus. The two bounded practice sessions apply the current agent card to the same educational toy.

roadmap_navigation.method: Locate the current skill; mark demonstrated understanding only; select one prerequisite gap. Maps are navigation, not the syllabus.

agent_practice_protocol.shared_artifact: Reuse one bounded synthetic toy or existing fixture harness, not a new weekly project.

practice_one.action: Reproduce the current guided concept from a manual trace or local stub; explain goal, observation, allowed action and stop condition on changed input.

practice_two.action: Exercise one refusal/failure case and one allowed case; compare expected and observed trace, then record a blocker and exact next action.

agent_practice_protocol.first_week: Manual traces are sufficient; company setup exceptions and exact reservations come only from private active authority.
agent_practice_protocol.implementation_gate: Use code only after its Python prerequisites are demonstrated. No paid API, external action, new framework or third project is required.

project_learning_strategy.foundation: Project 0 remains the single paired curriculum build: independent Python and Rust file-statistics CLIs. Transferable skills are explicit input/output contracts, error handling, meaningful tests, CLI use and reproducible runs; required acceptance fixtures remain unchanged.
project_learning_strategy.company: M.A.L. remains the primary company product experiment in its separate technical repository and company governance. Educational Rust priority does not change the current Python/scripted v0.2 implementation or company evidence.
project_learning_strategy.second_scenario: After synthetic supply-scheduling v0.2 acceptance, add synthetic virtual data-center maintenance as M.A.L. scenario two, reusing evaluator, event ledger, comparison report and replay. This is not a new parallel product.
project_learning_strategy.service_decision: A standalone evaluation service remains a hypothesis until reproducible technical evidence and discovery establish a repeated costly workflow, engaged engineering owner, credible budget owner and bounded delivery effort. Use existing company decisions; no new curriculum gate.
